items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 173:1
items.html: The point of the conclusion of the direct lights, that is, the line of the Ein Sof, is also the point of the conclusion of the circles and of the direct [lights] of the surroundings, both in the first restriction and in the second restriction. Only the difference is that in the direct lights the point of the conclusion is found below, and there it holds back the light from expanding further. But in the surrounding lights the point of the conclusion is found in their center, in such a way that the innermost circle of the surroundings, which is their last, surrounds the point that concludes the direct [lights]; and the place of the point is the aspect of an empty void, both of the inner lights and of the surrounding lights. (Item 4).
